name: dns-wildcard-san-tld-constraint-valid
description: permittedSubtrees dNSName is 'com' (a single-label TLD constraint). The leaf's dNSName SAN is '*.example.com'. RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10 defines DNS constraint matching as suffix-based: any name that adds zero-or-more labels to the left of the constraint is permitted. Every expansion of '*.example.com' is of the form '<label>.example.com', which has 'com' as a proper suffix and therefore falls inside the permitted subtree. The leaf must be accepted under the strict subset relation that BoringSSL's wildcard handling encodes: the wildcard's right-hand sequence ('example.com') is itself inside the constraint, so every possible expansion is too.
notes: TLD-shaped constraints ('com', 'net', etc.) are unusual but legal under RFC 5280; the spec doesn't constrain how few labels a permitted-subtree DNS name can carry. This case is interesting because some validators reject single-label DNS constraints out of suspicion (RFC 5280 doesn't require this, but several implementations do), and the wildcard SAN makes the interaction harder still — the validator has to compute 'is every expansion of *.example.com inside the com subtree?' and answer yes.
